title: Companies That Sponsor H-1B for New Grads (2027 List)
summary: International students: how CPT, OPT, STEM OPT and the wage-weighted visa lottery work in 2027, which employers file the most petitions, and how many early-career openings on Simplify offer support.
body_markdown:
The companies that sponsor the most H-1B visas for new hires are big tech firms (Amazon, Google, Meta, Microsoft, Apple), IT services firms (Infosys, Tata Consultancy Services, Cognizant) and the large consulting firms. But a company filing H-1Bs is not a promise that it will sponsor you, for your role, this year. On Simplify today, only 684 of about 410,000 open US internship and entry-level postings say sponsorship is or may be available, and most say nothing at all.


I came to the US at 19 for college, and I'm the first person in my family to study abroad. Every application I sent, I figured out on my own, and the visa rules are still scattered across a dozen government pages. So this post puts the whole path in one place: the work permits you get as a student, how the new H-1B lottery works, which employers file the most, and what we see in Simplify's own job data.


I'm not an immigration lawyer. Confirm anything about your own status with your school's international student office (your DSO) before you act on it.


## How do international students get from F-1 to H-1B?


Most students on an F-1 visa go through the same four steps. Together they let you work while your employer tries for an H-1B.


Step What it is How long Who approves it


**CPT** (Curricular Practical Training) Work that is part of your degree, like a required internship or co-op While you're enrolled Your school's DSO


**OPT** (Optional Practical Training) Work in your field during or after your degree Up to 12 months per degree level USCIS, after your DSO recommends it


**STEM OPT** An extension of OPT for STEM degrees 24 more months USCIS; the employer must use E-Verify


**H-1B** A work visa your employer applies for through a lottery 3 years, renewable once USCIS, after a lottery selection


A few rules that trip people up:


- **Full-time CPT can cost you OPT.** If you do 12 months or more of full-time CPT, you lose OPT eligibility at that degree level ([Study in the States](https://studyinthestates.dhs.gov/sevis-help-hub/student-records/fm-student-employment/curricular-practical-training-cpt?ref=blog.simplify.jobs) ). Part-time CPT doesn't count toward that. Ask your DSO how your school applies it.
- **OPT timing matters.** You can apply for post-completion OPT up to 90 days before your program ends and no later than 60 days after, per[USCIS](https://www.uscis.gov/working-in-the-united-states/students-and-exchange-visitors/optional-practical-training-opt-for-f-1-students?ref=blog.simplify.jobs) . Any OPT you use before graduating comes out of the 12 months.
- **STEM OPT is the big one.** 12 months of OPT plus 24 months of STEM OPT gives you up to three H-1B lottery tries instead of one. Check whether your degree's CIP code is on the STEM list before you assume it isn't.
- **Cap-gap covers the summer.** If your employer files an H-1B petition for you on time and your OPT ends before October 1, a cap-gap extension can keep you working until the H-1B starts.


## How does the H-1B lottery work for new grads in 2027?


There are 85,000 new cap H-1Bs each year: 65,000 regular and 20,000 more for people with a US master's degree or higher (the "master's cap"). Your employer registers you in March for $215, not you. If you hold a US master's, you're entered in the regular draw first, and if you aren't picked, you get a second chance in the master's draw.


**The big change: the lottery is now weighted by salary.** DHS published the final rule in the[Federal Register on December 29, 2025](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2025-12-29/html/2025-23853.htm?ref=blog.simplify.jobs) . It took effect February 27, 2026, and the FY 2027 registration in March 2026 was the first one run this way. USCIS[announced on March 31, 2026](https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/USDHSCIS/bulletins/410e914?ref=blog.simplify.jobs) that it had enough registrations to fill both the regular cap and the master's cap.


Each registration is placed in a wage level based on the offered salary, the job's occupation code and the work location. Higher levels get more entries:


Wage level Entries in the lottery DHS projected selection chance


Level I 1 about 15%


Level II 2 about 31%


Level III 3 over 45%


Level IV 4 over 61%


Those percentages are the department's projections in the rule, not results. USCIS hasn't published actual FY 2027 odds by level. Because levels depend on location, the same salary can land in a lower level in San Francisco than in a lower-cost city. Ask your employer which level they plan to file at.


You may also have heard about a $100,000 payment on some new H-1B petitions. As of October 7, 2026, courts had blocked collection, the government's appeal was still pending, and the fee was aimed at people outside the US ([University of Colorado ISSS](https://www.colorado.edu/isss/2026/10/07/100000-h-1b-fee-current-status?ref=blog.simplify.jobs) ). This is one to check again with your international office before you file.

It's the most recent complete year USCIS offers as a downloadable file. Two things to know before you use this list. IT services firms like Infosys and Cognizant file a lot, but many of those approvals are for experienced hires they bring in, so they are not the same as new grad openings. And the Data Hub's interactive view now runs through fiscal year 2026, so look up any company you're serious about there before you apply. It's free, and I used it for my post on[lesser-known Chinese-friendly companies in the US](https://simplify.jobs/blog/chinese-friendly-companies-us?ref=blog.simplify.jobs) , where it showed small employers that sponsor more than you'd guess.


## Which companies sponsor H-1B for entry-level jobs right now?


The USCIS data is a few years old and covers everyone, so I also looked at what's open today: every US internship and entry-level full-time posting open on Simplify on November 25, 2026, about 410,000 in total, and checked what each one says about sponsorship.


What the posting says Share of postings Internships Entry-level full-time


Sponsorship is or may be available 0.17% (684) 0.59% 0.12%


No sponsorship 8.0% 22.6% 6.5%


Nothing either way 91.8% 76.8% 93.4%


A few things stood out to me:


- **Silence is the norm.** More than 9 in 10 postings don't mention sponsorship. That isn't a no. It means you have to ask.
- **Internships say no more often.** Almost a quarter of internship postings rule out sponsorship, compared with about 1 in 15 entry-level jobs. If you're on CPT, read the fine print before you apply.
- **Sponsoring companies are easier to find than sponsoring postings.** 3.8% of these postings, and 14.9% of internships, are at companies Simplify marks as having sponsored H-1Bs in the past. That's more than 20 times as many as the postings that say so themselves.


These are the companies with the most open US internship and entry-level postings that say sponsorship is or may be available:


Company Postings Typical roles


Albertsons 77 Pharmacy interns


Reliant Rehabilitation 44 Physical and occupational therapists


Zoetis 43 Lab and manufacturing technicians


Schreiber Foods 33 Plant and operations roles


Rochester Regional Health 28 Physicians and nurse practitioners


Fab2 18 Engineering interns

EY 17 Tax analysts and consulting interns


SportsMed Physical Therapy 17 Physical therapists

Healthcare employers make up most of this list, and many of their postings say "visa sponsorship available" in the benefits section. For tech and business roles, Verkada (13), Deloitte (13) and Optiver (6) had the most. How I counted: postings open and visible on Simplify, located in the US, either internships or full-time roles tagged entry level. "Say sponsorship is available" means our parser read the posting text that way, often phrased "may be available," so treat it as a lead, not a guarantee.


## Does filing H-1Bs mean a company will sponsor you?


No, and I'll keep repeating this. A company's H-1B record tells you it *can* sponsor and has done it before. It doesn't tell you:


- whether **this team or office** sponsors (policies differ by role, office and level),
- whether they sponsor **new grads** , or only experienced hires,
- whether they **refile** if you aren't picked the first year,
- or whether this year's budget includes it.


The only way to know is to ask. Do it early, before you spend weeks on interviews.


## What about consulting firms?


Consulting recruiting has its own unwritten rules for international students. A few that still hold:


- **Strategy arms recruit separately.**[EY-Parthenon](https://www.ey.com/en_us/strategy/ey-parthenon?ref=blog.simplify.jobs) runs its own process apart from EY, and[Strategy&](https://www.strategyand.pwc.com/?ref=blog.simplify.jobs) apart from PwC. Apply through the wrong channel and you may not be considered for the strategy role at all. Our[MBB vs Big 4 vs boutique consulting comparison](https://simplify.jobs/blog/mbb-vs-big-4-boutique-consulting?ref=blog.simplify.jobs) explains how those recruiting channels differ.
- **Sponsorship differs by firm and office.** In the same FY 2022 USCIS data, Deloitte had 1,169 new H-1B approvals, EY 702, McKinsey 481, BCG 229, PwC 181, KPMG 140 and Bain 76.
- **Ask the recruiter directly.** When you get a call with a recruiter or an alum, ask: "Does this office sponsor H-1B for this role, and do you refile if I'm not selected the first year?" The answer to the second half changes how many lottery tries you get.
- **Answer the two application questions truthfully.** On OPT you're usually authorized to work now (yes), and you'll need sponsorship later (also yes). Firms that don't sponsor screen you out there, which saves you time.


## How to find H-1B sponsor jobs on Simplify


1. **Start with the list.**[New Grad Roles with Visa Sponsorship](https://simplify.jobs/l/New-Grad-Roles-with-Visa-Sponsorship?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=cta&utm_campaign=companies-that-sponsor-h1b-new-grads&utm_content=body-1) is a curated list of entry-level and new grad roles where sponsorship may be available. Our team reviews each job before it's added, and the list updates hourly.
2. **Turn on the "Sponsors H1B" filter** in Simplify's job search, then add your own filters for role, location and experience level. The filter also shows roles at companies that have sponsored H-1Bs before, even when the posting itself doesn't say so.
3. **Read the posting anyway.** The flag is a research signal. Some postings say "no sponsorship" even at companies with a long H-1B record.
4. **Write down what each company told you.** In the free[Job Tracker](https://simplify.jobs/job-application-tracker?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=cta&utm_campaign=companies-that-sponsor-h1b-new-grads&utm_content=body-2) , add a note to each application with what the recruiter said about sponsorship and refiling, so you aren't guessing three months later.
5. **Apply faster.**[Simplify Copilot](https://simplify.jobs/copilot?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=cta&utm_campaign=companies-that-sponsor-h1b-new-grads&utm_content=body-3) is a free Chrome extension that autofills applications. You still review and submit each one yourself, so check the two work authorization answers every time.


Simplify is used by more than 2 million job seekers. In a 2022 survey of Harvard CS students it ranked among the top three places they found tech internships ([Harvard career center, archived](https://web.archive.org/web/20240228134502/https://careerservices.fas.harvard.edu/blog/2022/11/22/beyond-big-tech-where-can-i-find-summer-opportunities/) ), and the University of Washington's career center[recommends it](https://careers.uw.edu/resources/simplify/?ref=blog.simplify.jobs) for applying faster.


## Common questions


**Which companies sponsor H-1B for new grads?** Large tech companies, IT services firms and big consulting firms file the most. In USCIS's FY 2022 data, Amazon, Infosys, Tata Consultancy Services, Cognizant, Google and Meta led on new H-1B approvals. On Simplify on November 25, 2026, the companies with the most open US internship and entry-level postings that say sponsorship may be available were Albertsons (77), Reliant Rehabilitation (44) and Zoetis (43).


**How do international students find jobs after graduating from a US university?** Use OPT (12 months) and, with a STEM degree, STEM OPT (24 more months) to work while your employer enters you in the H-1B lottery. Target employers with an H-1B record, filter for sponsorship, and ask each recruiter early whether the role sponsors.


**Can I do an internship on CPT and still get OPT?** Yes, as long as you stay under 12 months of full-time CPT at that degree level. Part-time CPT doesn't count toward that limit. Your DSO authorizes CPT, so check with them first.


**How does the weighted H-1B lottery work?** Since the FY 2027 registration in March 2026, each registration is entered one to four times based on the job's wage level, so higher-paid offers get better odds. DHS projected about a 15% chance at Level I and over 61% at Level IV.


**Does a US master's degree help in the H-1B lottery?** Yes. Master's holders are entered in the 65,000 regular draw first and, if not picked, get a second chance at the 20,000 master's cap.
